AccessConfig.description:
The access policy (``runtime/acl.py``) selected by name; no class is loaded from config.

* ``none``: every principal sees the whole dataset (single-tenant serving, the default).
* ``tenant``: every arm, tool, value listing and graph read is restricted to records whose
  ``field`` equals the principal's ``tenant``. A principal without a tenant sees nothing
  (fail closed) unless its id is listed in ``unrestricted`` (an operator).
AccessConfig.title: AccessConfig

AccountingConfig.description:
Line accounting (addendum A2 §4.2.1): ``required_fields`` maps a signature category to the
fields a ``parsed`` line of that category must carry with a valid value; a line an approved
pattern matched without one is a field gap (``learning.extraction.fill``).
AccountingConfig.title: AccountingConfig

ActionsConfig.description:
Write actions (plan §3.4). Default: none. Only built-in actions named here are registered;
every invocation (also a denied one) is audited on ``storage.ledger`` before it runs.
ActionsConfig.title: ActionsConfig

Bm25Settings.description:
Okapi BM25 lexical engine (``lexical_engine: bm25``), the formula of ``rank_bm25.BM25Okapi``:
ATIRE idf ``log(N - df + 0.5) - log(df + 0.5)`` with negative idf replaced by
``epsilon * mean(idf)``. ``tokenizer``: ``unicode_word`` = ``\w+`` runs, ``ascii_alnum`` =
``[a-z0-9]+`` runs of the lower-cased text. ``stemming``: ``none`` or a Snowball algorithm name.
``include_title``: the document title's tokens are prepended to every chunk of the document.
All of it is index recipe: changing any value needs a rebuild.
Bm25Settings.title: Bm25Settings

BootstrapConfig.description:
``learning.bootstrap`` (A2 rev 4): the first ``days`` days of the fallback, when the residue
backlog is largest. Off by default. While active, cluster calls go to self-hosted routes only
(``local``/``lan``; paid routes are skipped) and are capped at ``max_clusters_per_day``.
``require_measured_throughput`` (default) refuses to start unless ``patterns measure-throughput``
has recorded a self-hosted tier, and the cap is then also bounded by the measured calls/hour over
``hours_per_day``. ``max_usd_per_day`` is required (finite) when a paid route can be reached.
BootstrapConfig.title: BootstrapConfig

CapabilityDeclaration.description:
What a chat role relies on; validated against ``providers/capabilities.py``.

``structured_output``: ``none`` (schema in the system prompt, strict validation of the
reply), ``json_mode`` (``response_format: json_object``; OpenAI-style providers only),
``json_schema`` (``response_format: json_schema``, ``strict: false``; OpenAI-style providers
only), ``native`` (provider-enforced: Anthropic forced tool use or ``output_config.format``,
OpenAI strict json_schema; only for registry-declared ``(provider, model)`` pairs). When a role
does not set ``structured_output``, Anthropic models the registry declares capable get
``native`` (2.0.0a3); every other role gets ``none``. ``prompt_caching``: ``controlled`` sends
``cache_control`` (Anthropic); ``passive`` records cached tokens the provider reports.
CapabilityDeclaration.title: CapabilityDeclaration

CoFiringConfig.description:
Co-firing communities (addendum A2 §4.1.4, A1 N6): signatures that fire together in hourly
cells. A cell is ``(tenant, env, hour)`` (``tenant_env_hour``, default; review N8), ``(deployment, hour)``
(``deployment_hour``, format-2 cells) or ``(tenant, env,
service, hour)`` (``service_hour``). Communities are computed **per tenant** (review B4), so an
incident never mixes tenants.
CoFiringConfig.title: CoFiringConfig

CommunityHierarchy.description:
``louvain_hierarchical``: level 0 is the coarsest partition; each level-``n`` community with at
least ``min_split`` documents is re-partitioned (seeded) into level ``n+1`` children.
CommunityHierarchy.title: CommunityHierarchy

CommunityStats.description: Deterministic per-community statistics from declared fields only (``communities/stats.py``).
CommunityStats.title: CommunityStats

ComposeKinds.description:
Analytics kinds composed from format-2 partitions (addendum A2 §4.1.1–4.1.2). Off by default
so a generic logs config composes exactly what it did; the ``logs_example`` profile turns them on.
ComposeKinds.title: ComposeKinds

CountQueryConfig.description:
A named count query. Built **per index from its mapping**: a ``level_field`` terms query on
``mapping.level`` where that field exists in the index, and otherwise a ``token_match`` query on
the message field. Without ``tokens`` an index lacking the level field is a typed schema-drift
error, never a zero.
CountQueryConfig.title: CountQueryConfig

CustomRedactor.description:
A user redactor of the ``safe`` engine: a regular expression in the RE2 subset that passes
the ReDoS lint (validated at load), and what replaces each match. ``mask`` writes
``[REDACTED_<NAME>]``; ``hash`` writes ``[<NAME>:<12 hex>]``, a keyed sha256 of the match, so
equal values stay joinable without being readable.
CustomRedactor.title: CustomRedactor

ExactIdArm.description:
Exact identifier lookups (plan §3.8): ``alias_map`` is a YAML/JSON file ``{aliases: {alias:
canonical_id}}``; ``alias_fields`` are declared metadata fields whose values identify a record;
identifiers are recognised by the ``pattern`` of ``id`` fields in ``metadata_schema`` and by the
alias map's keys. Matching is exact (``casefold`` is the only normalisation, opt-in); an unknown
identifier is reported, never guessed.
ExactIdArm.title: ExactIdArm

ExtractionEgressConfig.description:
Egress of the fallback (A2 §4.2.4, N6): a line that still shows a PII shape after redaction is
``unresolved: egress_refused`` on its own and never sent; the whole run is refused only when the
refused share of the residue exceeds ``max_refused_share``.
ExtractionEgressConfig.title: ExtractionEgressConfig

ExtractionFallbackConfig.description:
``learning.extraction``: the LLM fallback for log lines the pattern library cannot parse or
parses without a required field (addendum A2 §4.2). It runs after a day partition is sealed and
writes a versioned **fallback overlay** next to it; the sealed partition is never changed.

``fields`` names the fields a model may label or quote, with their types (the closed set
below); a label or quote naming any other field is dropped. ``max_residue_lines`` caps the
residue queue per run; lines beyond it are ``unresolved: budget_deferred`` and reported.
``reply_cache`` defaults to ``<spend ledger dir>/.fallback_replies.sqlite``. Nothing here names
code.
ExtractionFallbackConfig.title: ExtractionFallbackConfig

FallbackBudgetConfig.description:
Spend caps of the ``log_extractor`` role (scope ``learning.extraction``): per run, per
calendar day and in total (persistent ledger; the day in ``timezone``). Provider lifetime caps
are ``budgets.providers.<provider>.max_usd_total``.
FallbackBudgetConfig.title: FallbackBudgetConfig

FieldValidatorConfig.description:
A value check for one field (A2 §4.2.4, N17): numeric ``min``/``max``, an ``enum`` or an
anchored ``regex`` (RE2 subset, linted). A value that fails it is ``range_invalid``.
FieldValidatorConfig.title: FieldValidatorConfig

FillFallbackConfig.description:
Missing-field fill (A2 §4.2.4) for lines an approved pattern matched without a valid value
for a field ``logs.accounting.required_fields`` requires: a cluster ``fix`` proposal first, then
at most ``max_per_day`` per-line quote calls.
FillFallbackConfig.title: FillFallbackConfig

GroundingFallbackConfig.description:
How a model quote is located in its line (``extraction/grounding.py``). ``relocated`` does
not exist for a single line and is refused; fuzzy matching does not exist at all. ``reject``
rejects an ambiguous quote unless the located text is identical at every occurrence.
GroundingFallbackConfig.title: GroundingFallbackConfig

HistoryConfig.description:
Serving window of derived data until the history tier (H1) lands: compose serves derived days
only within ``serve_days`` (default: the masked window, ``retention.keep_days``); older derived
snapshots stay archived for the history tier to import.
HistoryConfig.title: HistoryConfig

IdentifierPin.description:
Lexical front policy (off by default): documents named by an identifier in the query lead the
lexical list. Identifiers are matches of the ``pattern`` of ``id`` fields in ``metadata_schema``
(``fields`` narrows which; empty = all) and resolve by exact equality on that document field
inside the request's scope. No normalisation, no fuzzy match; at most ``max_records``.
IdentifierPin.title: IdentifierPin

IndexNameConfig.description:
Index-name grammar: ``[<prefix>-][<deployment prefix>-]<prefix fields>-<service>-<date>``
(``deployment_position: leading``) or ``[<prefix>-]<prefix fields>-[<deployment prefix>-]<service>-<date>``
(``deployment_position: before_service``).

- ``date_format`` matches the trailing date (``%Y``, ``%m``, ``%d`` and literal separators).
- ``prefix`` (optional) is a literal every name must start with, followed by ``separator``. It
  is stripped before the segments are read, so it never becomes part of the first prefix field
  (``prefix: logs`` reads ``logs-acme-prod-crawler-…`` as tenant ``acme``).
- ``deployment_prefixes`` (optional) are deployment or infrastructure prefixes, tried longest
  first; ``{n}`` stands for a run of digits (``os-data-{n}`` matches ``os-data-1``). A matched
  prefix is recorded as the ``deployment`` attribute (``none`` when the name has none).
  ``deployment_position`` says where they stand: at the left of the prefix fields (``leading``,
  the default) or between the prefix fields and the service (``before_service``). ``after_env``
  is env-anchored and needs no list: the deployment is whatever lies between the last prefix
  field (matched by its vocabulary) and the service (matched by its vocabulary).
- ``prefix_fields`` (default ``tenant``, ``env``) and ``service`` are the segments. A segment
  with a vocabulary takes the **longest** vocabulary entry that fits (``query-gateway`` wins
  over ``gateway``); a segment without one is exactly one separator-free token, so service
  names such as ``slack_bot`` parse with the ``-`` separator.

A name that does not fit the grammar, or that fits it in more than one way (with and without
a deployment prefix), is ``unparsed`` with a typed reason and ``unknown`` attributes: never a
guess.
IndexNameConfig.title: IndexNameConfig

IngestBudget.description:
Limits of one ingestion build (the write path), separate from the per-request limits.

``max_llm_calls`` caps extraction and community-report calls of the whole build;
``max_embedding_calls`` caps embedding provider requests (one per batch of
``models.roles.embedder.batch_size`` chunks; reused vectors cost none); ``max_usd`` caps the
build's spend across both, reserved before every call from ``budgets.price_table`` and
committed with the reported usage. Exhaustion stops the stage (``budget`` category) under the
extraction policy; nothing is downgraded or retried.
IngestBudget.title: IngestBudget

KuzuAttach.description:
Read-only attachment of an existing Kuzu database: ``mapping`` is a YAML file that maps its node
and relationship tables onto the graph contract (``backends/kuzu/attach.py``). Private mappings
stay outside the repository; the path is relative to this config file.
KuzuAttach.title: KuzuAttach

LineFallbackConfig.description:
Capped per-line tail (A2 §4.2.4): singletons and lines whose provisional application failed
alignment, at most ``max_per_day`` lines per run in batches of ``batch_size`` lines of one
``(service, level)``; lines longer than ``max_line_chars`` are never sent.
LineFallbackConfig.title: LineFallbackConfig

LineRecipeConfig.description:
``ingestion.line_recipe``: the ``line`` chunk recipe (addendum §3.4.2 n1). Each listed field is
cut into one chunk per log record (records are separated by one blank line), whatever
``chunking.size`` is, so a line-scoped fact never spans two chunks. A record longer than
``max_chunk_chars`` is a build error, never split.
LineRecipeConfig.title: LineRecipeConfig

LogFieldMap.description:
Which source fields become ``LogRecord`` fields. Only these (plus ``extra``) are requested
through ``_source`` includes; ``drop_fields`` are never requested.
LogFieldMap.title: LogFieldMap

LogIntentsConfig.description:
The typed log intents and tools (addendum A2 §4.1.5). ``enabled`` makes every decision agent
route recognised log questions through one typed intent step, and refuses free structured scopes
over the rollups (review B5).
LogIntentsConfig.title: LogIntentsConfig

LuceneRecordsConfig.description:
How the ``records`` facet evaluates a typed scope. ``client`` (default): the matched records are
scanned and the operations computed in Python, bounded by ``max_matched`` (typed refusal above
it). ``native``: the operations are compiled to aggregations on the server (no record scan);
``matched_ids`` then holds at most ``matched_ids_cap`` ids (``matched_ids_truncated`` above it), more
than ``max_groups`` groups is a ``bounded`` result, and ``count_distinct`` is exact up to
``distinct_exact_cap`` distinct values, ``approximate`` (engine ``cardinality``) above it. A query-time
setting: not part of the index recipe.
LuceneRecordsConfig.title: LuceneRecordsConfig

ModelRoute.description:
One provider route of a learning role (owner decision 2026-11-04: local models first).

``health_url`` is probed (HTTP GET, 2xx = ready) before the first call of a run; for an
``openai_compatible`` role it defaults to ``<base_url>/models``. ``capacity_url`` is an optional
second GET whose JSON ``{"available": true|false}`` (or a 2xx without a body) says whether the
server takes work now. A hosted route without a ``health_url`` is not probed. There is no probe
*command*: config never names code.
ModelRoute.title: ModelRoute

ModelRoutes.description:
Ordered provider routes per learning role (``pattern_learner``: cluster calls;
``log_extractor``: line and fill calls). The first available route is used; when none is
available the items are ``unresolved: capacity_deferred`` and the next run retries them. A paid
(non-loopback) route after a local one is used only with ``allow_paid_fallback: true``. Empty
lists mean the single route ``models.roles.<role>``.
ModelRoutes.title: ModelRoutes

MultilineConfig.description:
Join continuation documents (stack frames, ``Caused by:``, column-0 Python tracebacks, lone
closing brackets …) onto the preceding head of the same ``(container, file)`` within
``max_gap_ms``. ``continuation`` names built-in rules (``sources/multiline.py``); the approved
``continuation`` entries of the pattern library are applied in addition wherever a library is
loaded (``logs`` pulls, ``patterns coverage|mine``).
MultilineConfig.title: MultilineConfig

NamedState.description: A declared name for a set of field values (``open`` = not ``done``/``closed``).
NamedState.title: NamedState

PackingConfig.description: Evidence budget with fair per-record allocation and a configured field priority.
PackingConfig.title: PackingConfig

PatternEgressConfig.description:
What may leave the process for the ``pattern_learner`` model.

Only lines processed by the configured ``privacy`` redaction are ever sent (anything else is
refused, not repaired). ``allow_hosted: false`` (the default) permits only an
``openai_compatible`` role on a loopback host. ``pseudonymise`` lists line attributes whose
values are replaced by stable per-run aliases (in the attributes and in the line text) before
the prompt is built.
PatternEgressConfig.title: PatternEgressConfig

PatternGateConfig.description: The deterministic validation gate a learned pattern must pass (``learning/patterns/gate.py``).
PatternGateConfig.title: PatternGateConfig

PatternLearningConfig.description:
``learning.patterns``: one ``patterns learn`` run mines the unparsed lines, asks
``pattern_learner`` about at most ``max_clusters_per_run`` clusters (each with at most
``max_lines_per_cluster`` example lines and ``nearest_patterns`` approved patterns), gates every
reply, writes the passing ones under the promotion policy and reports coverage before and after.

**Spend.** Every call is reserved before it is sent, against the run caps
(``max_calls_per_run``, ``max_usd_per_run``) and the persistent per-day caps
(``max_calls_per_day``, ``max_usd_per_day``; the day is the calendar day in ``timezone``). USD
caps need ``budgets.price_table``; a hosted role needs both USD caps. A refused reservation stops
the run; nothing is retried or downgraded. The ledger is ``spend_ledger`` (default
``<library>/.spend_ledger.sqlite``).
PatternLearningConfig.title: PatternLearningConfig

PatternLibraryRef.description:
``extraction.pattern_library``: the library directory of the ``pattern`` extractor.

Only ``engine``, ``max_line_bytes`` and ``mode`` enter the index recipe. The library contents,
the engine version and the promotion policy are build provenance (generation manifest), so a
library edit never changes the live fingerprint; it changes the extraction reuse salt instead.
PatternLibraryRef.title: PatternLibraryRef

PgVectorConfig.description:
pgvector search. ``exact`` (default) scans with the scope in the WHERE clause; ``hnsw`` builds
per-namespace HNSW indexes at refresh and fails the refresh when the measured filter recall
against exact search is below ``min_filter_recall``.
PgVectorConfig.title: PgVectorConfig

PipelineConfig.description:
One retrieval/answer pipeline. ``pipeline`` is the default (named ``default``); every entry of
``pipelines`` is an overlay deep-merged onto it before validation (an arm set to ``null`` is
disabled in that pipeline).
PipelineConfig.title: PipelineConfig

PrecomputedVectors.description:
Import document vectors computed elsewhere. ``vectors`` is a 2-D float32 ``.npy`` file;
``keys`` is a JSONL file with one object per row ``{"document_id", "field", "text_sha256"}``.

What is verified: both files' SHA-256 equal the pinned ``sha256`` (vectors) and ``keys_sha256``
(keys); row count, dimension, finite and non-zero rows, unique keys; and every chunk is matched
to a key by document, field and the SHA-256 of its exact text (never fuzzily). What is NOT
verifiable from the files alone: that row ``i`` of the vectors embeds the text named by line
``i`` of the keys. That pairing is positional; the two pinned digests fix the pair as published,
and ``verify`` (a re-embedding spot check with the configured provider) is the check that
detects a misaligned pair. Index identity comes from the two digests, never from file paths.
A chunk with no row is an error unless ``on_missing: embed``. Queries are always encoded by the
configured provider, which must be the model that produced the rows.
PrecomputedVectors.title: PrecomputedVectors

PrecomputedVerify.description:
Optional content check of imported rows: re-embed ``sample`` matched chunks (seeded, through
the configured provider with its ``document_prefix``) and require cosine ``>= min_cosine``
against the imported row for every sampled chunk. This is the only check that can detect a
vector row paired with the wrong key.

``input`` is what the producer embedded for a keyed chunk, and so what is re-embedded:
``engine_template`` (default) is the input the package's own embedder uses (``{title}\n{field}:
{text}``, ``ingestion.write.EMBEDDING_INPUT``; also what ``on_missing: embed`` embeds);
``chunk_text`` is the bare chunk text as keyed. A producer that used another template cannot be
spot-checked (set ``sample: 0``); the check never guesses.
PrecomputedVerify.title: PrecomputedVerify

PredicateDecl.description: Entity types a predicate may connect (empty = any).
PredicateDecl.title: PredicateDecl

PrivacyConfig.description:
Opt-in conservative redaction; not a complete PII detector.

``engine: legacy`` (default) is the a1/a2 behaviour: ``redact_emails`` and ``patterns`` with
Python ``re`` on documents. ``engine: safe`` (B11) runs the named built-in ``redactors``, the
``custom`` redactors and the ``patterns`` (as ``mask`` redactors) through the pattern engine's
validator (RE2 subset, ReDoS lint) and runtime (``regex_engine``: ``re2``, or the ``regex``
development engine with a per-call timeout that fails the redaction rather than skipping it).
It redacts log records before any persistence, ingested documents and every prompt line. The
new keys are omitted from every fingerprint while they hold their defaults.
PrivacyConfig.title: PrivacyConfig

ProjectionsConfig.description:
``ingestion.projections``: which document kinds stay out of a projection, and which fields of a
kind are embedded. Catalog and records always hold every document.
ProjectionsConfig.title: ProjectionsConfig

ProviderBudget.description:
A lifetime (total-period) USD cap for one provider key across every learning and extraction
scope (addendum A2 §4.2.6). Reservations persist in the learning spend ledger; reaching the cap
stops the step (``budget_deferred``), never a switch to another provider.
ProviderBudget.title: ProviderBudget

PullConfig.description: Records-tier pull: cursor, page size, keepalive bound and stratified caps (§3.1.3).
PullConfig.title: PullConfig

RawCopyConfig.description:
Optional raw-copy store (``ingestion/raw_store.py``): pulled units **unredacted**, so redaction
and parsing can be re-run without the source. Off by default; kept ``retention.raw_days``.
RawCopyConfig.title: RawCopyConfig

RetentionConfig.description:
Retention per data class.

- ``keep_days`` (alias ``partition_days``): the masked day partitions (records, matches, unparsed
  queue), the N most recent complete days.
- ``raw_days``: the raw-copy store (``partitions.raw``), shorter than ``keep_days``.
- ``derived``: the composed arm data (day and hour rollups, signature catalog and exemplars, graph,
  communities, the documents of every projection). ``window`` (default; the single-window
  behaviour): derived data follows the partitions. ``forever``: every composed day stays in the
  serving generation after its partition expired. An integer: days of derived data kept
  (at least ``keep_days``).
RetentionConfig.title: RetentionConfig

ServingAnswersSpend.description:
``serving.answers`` (addendum A2 rev 4): answer-time model calls (planner, generator,
reviewer) reserve on a persistent per-day ledger under their own scope ``serving.answers``,
separate from the learning scopes, and on ``budgets.providers.<provider>.max_usd_total`` when
the provider has one. Off by default (per-request ``budgets`` only). A refused reservation fails
the call before it is sent; there is no fallback to another provider.
ServingAnswersSpend.title: ServingAnswersSpend

SessionBudget.description:
Cumulative limits over every turn of one session; each request's limits are clipped to what
the session has left, and an exhausted session refuses further turns (``BudgetExhausted``).
SessionBudget.title: SessionBudget

SourceConfig.description:
One read-only log source. ``kind: elasticsearch_rest`` covers Elasticsearch ≥ 7.9 and
OpenSearch ≥ 1.0 over plain REST (older 7.x discover through ``/{expr}/_alias``).
SourceConfig.title: SourceConfig

StagePolicies.description: Outcome of a failed stage inside a ``cascade`` (plan §3.7.1 rows "cascade stage").
StagePolicies.title: StagePolicies

StorageConfig.description: Authoritative backend per non-arm capability; each must name exactly one backend declaring it.
StorageConfig.title: StorageConfig

TemplateFallbackConfig.description:
Cluster-first fallback (A2 §4.2.3): one ``pattern_learner`` call per residue cluster of at
least ``min_support`` lines, at most ``max_clusters_per_day`` clusters per run (ranked by size x
level weight), each prompt with at most ``max_lines_per_prompt`` lines. Calls reserve against
``learning.patterns`` (scope ``learning.patterns``). ``write_proposals`` writes passing entries
through the existing promotion policy (``learned.yaml`` + ``approve`` under ``auto``, otherwise
``proposed.yaml``).
TemplateFallbackConfig.title: TemplateFallbackConfig

ToolsConfig.description:
Read-only tools exposed through the engine (plan §3.4). Only registered components can be
named: the built-ins; there is no code loading from config.
ToolsConfig.title: ToolsConfig

UiConfig.description:
The static web UI (addendum A2 §4.4; wheel ``su-multi-arm-ui``). ``enabled`` mounts it at
``mount`` on the HTTP app; without the wheel the server refuses to start (``ConfigError``). The
UI needs bearer auth (or an injected resolver) unless ``allow_unauthenticated_loopback`` is set
explicitly for single-user development.
UiConfig.title: UiConfig

VerbatimBoost.description:
Lexical front policy (off by default): documents whose text holds a quoted string of the query,
or at least ``min_windows`` of its ``window_tokens``-token windows verbatim (error messages, pasted
excerpts, exact subjects), lead the lexical list, at most ``max_records``, ranked by (quoted,
windows matched). A window counts only if one of its tokens is in at most ``common_df`` chunks; a
window found in more than ``max_window_hits`` chunks is boilerplate and ignored; a window whose
tokens co-occur in more than ``max_candidates`` chunks is not verified (skipped, counted in the
trace). Needs a lexical index that exposes its analyzer and term statistics (sqlite
``lexical_engine: bm25``); anything else is a validation error.
VerbatimBoost.title: VerbatimBoost
